newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem lashes out at "tyrant" Castro.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem lashes out at "tyrant" Castro.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem, a long-standing critic of Fidel Castro, lashed out more harshly than ever against the Cuban leader on Monday, saying his latest clash with Spain showed he was still a "tyrant."

Speaking to foreign journalists on the eve of a visit to the United States where he will meet President Bill Clinton, the Peronist president showed he was fully in favour of Spain and the European Union taking a tougher line against Castro.

"If I justify even tangentially the Cuban government, I justify all tyrannies of recent times, not just in Argentina but in all the countries of the world," said Menem. "To justify Fidel Castro is to justify all tyrants."

Menem, who said he would discuss Cuba with Clinton when they meet in Washington on Thursday, joked that he hoped Castro's recent audience with Pope John Paul II in the Vatican "will convert him to Christianity and to democracy."

After the United States spent months criticising Europe for its "spineless" stance on Cuba in opposing ever-tougher U.S. sanctions on the communist island, the U.S. State Department was now praising Spain for taking a new hard line.
Madrid, which was accused last week of meddling in Cuba's affairs and saw approval for its new ambassador withdrawn, was nudging its EU partners to press harder for democracy in Cuba.

Menem said the dispute between Havana and Madrid -- which got along well with Castro under 13 years of Socialist rule but has now changed its tune under conservative Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar -- "shows clearly the 'commandante' doesn't want to install democracy or liberty or respect for human rights in the island."

In the past Menem has compared Castro to the military juntas that ruled Argentina for much of this century. But at the same time, like other Latin American leaders, he opposes trade sanctions that are strangling the island's economy.
